title: Thomas Edison: Inventor and Busy Team Leader

source.name: VOA Learning English — Thomas Edison: Inventor and Busy Team Leader
source.license: Nội dung của VOA (Voice of America), phạm vi công cộng
source.note: Đã rút gọn: chỉ giữ một số đoạn.

paras: The inventor Thomas Alva Edison had a major effect on the lives of people around the world. Thomas Edison is remembered most for the electric light, his phonograph, and his work with motion pictures.
Edison was born on February 11, 1847, in Milan, Ohio. He was mostly self-taught. His mother taught him reading, writing, and mathematics. He learned from books, and he experimented.
At the age of 10, he experimented with chemicals and electricity. He built a telegraph machine and, at the age of 16, he went to work as a telegraph operator.
He continued his work with electricity, making improved telegraph machines, and he invented an electrical voting machine.

Edison earned enough money from his early inventions to start his own company in 1871. Instead of working alone, he worked with a group of employees on many different projects at one time. They asked the United States government for patents to protect more than one hundred devices or inventions each year. He was an extremely busy man.
In 1913, a popular magazine at the time called Thomas Edison the most useful man in America.
He almost never slept more than four or five hours a night. He usually worked 18 hours each day because he enjoyed what he was doing.

A reporter asked Edison in 1917 which of his many inventions he enjoyed the most. He answered, the phonograph was really the most interesting. The hardest invention to develop, he said, was the electric light. He said that it was the most difficult and the most important. He also invented the modern motion picture film.

In 1928, he received a special medal of honor from the Congress of the United States. Thomas Edison died on January 6, 1931. People worldwide have had easier and more enjoyable lives because of his inventions.

questions.q: How did Edison mainly receive his education?
options: At a technical college, where he studied electricity for years
Mostly through his own reading and tests, after early lessons at home
By serving as an apprentice to a well-known inventor
From evening lectures given by the telegraph company
questions.explain: Đoạn 2: tự học là chính; mẹ dạy đọc, viết, toán; học từ sách và thí nghiệm.

questions.q: What was different about the way Edison worked after 1871?
options: He concentrated on one invention until it was finished
He stopped inventing and spent his time running a business
He worked alone so that he could protect his patents
He directed a team that handled several projects at once
questions.explain: Đoạn 5: lập công ty, làm việc với nhóm nhân viên, nhiều dự án cùng lúc.

questions.q: What does the writer use to show how productive Edison’s group was?
options: The number of patent applications it made each year
The prizes it won from scientific magazines
The size of the factory that it built in Ohio
The profits it made from selling electric lights
questions.explain: Đoạn 5: nhóm xin bằng sáng chế cho hơn một trăm thiết bị/phát minh mỗi năm.

questions.q: How did Edison compare his own inventions in 1917?
options: The electric light was the most enjoyable and the phonograph the hardest
The phonograph interested him most, but the electric light was the hardest
Motion pictures were both the hardest and the most important
All of his inventions had been equally difficult to develop
questions.explain: Đoạn 8: máy hát là thú vị nhất; bóng đèn điện khó nhất (và quan trọng nhất).

questions.q: What does the writer suggest about Edison’s very long working days?
options: They did not trouble him because he liked what he did
His employers demanded them from everyone in the company
They damaged his health in his later years
They were a condition for receiving government patents
questions.explain: Đoạn 7: làm 18 giờ mỗi ngày “because he enjoyed what he was doing”.

questions.q: Which statement best sums up the writer’s final judgement?
options: He was admired more abroad than in his own country at the time
His business success mattered more to the world than his inventions
His inventions made everyday life easier and more pleasant for people
His work was valued only by scientists and professional engineers
questions.explain: Đoạn 9: nhờ phát minh của ông, người dân trên thế giới có cuộc sống dễ dàng và thú vị hơn.

questions.q: Edison was still in his twenties when he started his own company.
questions.explain: Đoạn 2 và 5: sinh năm 1847, lập công ty năm 1871 → khoảng 23–24 tuổi.

questions.q: Edison’s was the first company in America to employ a team of inventors.
questions.explain: Bài chỉ nói ông làm việc với một nhóm nhân viên; không nói đó là công ty đầu tiên như vậy.
